The data can't settle this. Only 2 of the 16,384 patients have R T3 radiculopathy, and neither has L arch pain. The cross-tabulation is too sparse to show either a dependence or a direction.

I'm relying on domain knowledge instead. In this neuropathic pain diagnostic network, radiculopathy is a pathophysiological diagnosis and pain is the symptom it produces. So the more likely direction is R T3 radiculopathy causing L arch pain. A pain symptom would not cause a nerve-root lesion.

ANSWER: A
